technical_and_design_decisions: Target projects are Spring Cloud Data Flow (s-c-d) and Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) on the Java 17+ baseline required by Spring Framework 6.
Kafka and Rabbit test @Rule fixtures will be extracted into separate publishable Gradle projects and consumed as test-scoped Maven/Gradle dependencies.
A PlatformAdminClient abstraction will be introduced so that Lattice, YARN, and CF share a common REST API contract, leveraging existing Spring Cloud Deployer SPI.
Library support will extend the existing AppRegistration model with a new Library type rather than creating a separate registry.
Named channels will be supported via an extended stream definition DSL using ':channelName:' syntax, relaxing the mandatory source/sink validation.
Duplicate stream name prevention will be enforced with a DB unique constraint plus a service-layer pre-check returning HTTP 409.
Kinesis source will be implemented as a Spring Cloud Stream source app using the existing AWS Kinesis binder, packaged as a SCDF app starter.
API contract tests for StreamController will use Spring MockMvc and Spring REST Docs executed at build time.
Gradle and GitHub Actions will be used for builds and CI.
assumptions: s-c-d stands for Spring Cloud Data Flow and s-c-s stands for Spring Cloud Stream.
Existing Kafka and Rabbit @Rule test fixtures already exist in the current codebase and can be cleanly extracted.
Lattice, YARN, and CF deployers already exist; only REST API consistency needs to be added.
The developer has sufficient permissions to create new repositories and publish artifacts to the organization's Maven repository.
Include/exclude statements refer to existing SCDF stream/app definition mechanisms.
Placeholders like {{@Rule}}, {{StreamController}}, {{kinesis}}, {{source}} refer to existing concrete classes/modules in the codebase.
Effort estimates are for a single experienced Spring developer and exclude external review delays and unrelated production incidents.
One workday equals 8 hours of focused development effort.
